title: Design System: Where did my money go

display.purpose: Selected month title only; 26px at 720px and below.

lede.purpose: The verdict sentence, max 62ch, ink-2 with bold coloured figures; 18px on mobile.

figure.purpose: Lead number in each insight row, coloured by tone.

title-sm.purpose: Panel titles inside sections, footer headings, wordmark.

body.purpose: Prose and table cells, tabular figures; 14px on mobile.

label.purpose: Table headers, pills, figure notes, field labels; sentence case.

axis.purpose: Chart axis and scale labels in ink-3, compact rupees.

mono.purpose: Raw bank narration text in the transactions table only.

categoryColor.purpose: Small marks only (swatch, share bar, sparkline selection, flow nodes), always beside the category name.

focus.rowVariant: box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--jade) on the leading cell, surface-2 fill

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every transition and animation.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover, press, selection colour and fill changes (120ms on table rows and weekday bars).

motion.name: swap
motion.purpose: Panels re-rendered on month change fade from 0.4 opacity and rise 3px.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes the swap animation and zeroes all transition durations.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Two-column grids and footer stack to one column.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Type steps down, optional columns hide, mobile meta lines appear, wordmark text hides.

narrative.overview:
The system reads like a sharp analyst talking you through your own month: a sentence first, then the comparison table that proves it, then the charts that let you check the working. Everything sits on a cool, faintly green paper-white ground in graphite ink. Structure comes from hairline rules and whitespace, not from boxed cards; the page is one continuous sheet divided into sections by single horizontal rules.

Colour is spent like money in a careful budget. Neutrals carry almost all of the page. One jade accent marks the thing you are looking at (the selected month, the active control's focus ring) and the money you kept. Persimmon appears only where money went wrong. Data series rest in low-chroma tints and only saturate for the selected month, so the eye always lands on "this month" first. Charts are hand-drawn SVG sharing one ₹ scale, typeset in the same face as the prose.

Anek Latin, with its native ₹ and tabular figures switched on everywhere, gives the numbers a single consistent rhythm. Indian money conventions are typographic rules here, not localisation: lakh grouping, `L` and `Cr` abbreviations, a true minus sign. The world is light-only; there is no dark theme.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper-white ground (hue 165) with graphite ink (hue 175); neutrals do the work.
Hairline rules instead of cards; sections separated by one 1px rule.
A single jade accent for selection and kept money; persimmon reserved for overspend.
Words and comparison tables lead; charts support and double as controls.
Tabular figures and Indian number formatting on every number, including inside SVG.
Flat at rest; only floating things (tooltip, toast) cast shadows.

rules.name: The One Jade Rule
rules.body: Jade means "selected" or "kept". It never decorates; if a jade element is neither the current selection, a focus state, nor money the owner kept or saved, it is the wrong colour.

rules.name: The Persimmon Is Overspend Rule
rules.body: Persimmon appears only where money went the wrong way or something failed. It is never a second brand accent.

rules.name: The Triangle-Plus-Tint Rule
rules.body: Colour encodes good or bad, a filled SVG triangle encodes up or down, and screen-reader text says "up" or "down". Spending up is a persimmon up-triangle; spending down is a jade down-triangle. Colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Muted-Until-Selected Rule
rules.body: Chart series rest in low-chroma tints; only the selected month takes the saturated `-sel` variants and the jade-wash column behind it.

rules.name: The Tabular Everywhere Rule
rules.body: `tnum` is set on the body and on every SVG `text`; any new number, in prose, table or chart, inherits it. Never switch to proportional figures for a "nicer" headline number.

rules.name: The Indian Money Rule
rules.body: Rupees always carry the ₹ sign with en-IN lakh grouping (₹1,78,974). Compact values use `k`, `L` and `Cr` (₹5.8k, ₹4 L, ₹1.2 Cr). Negatives use a true minus (−), missing values an em dash (—).

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, header, tag and button is sentence case at normal tracking. Hierarchy comes from size and weight steps, not from capitals or letterspacing.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Box Rule
rules.body: Analysis lives on the open sheet, divided by 1px rules. Bordered or tinted containers are reserved for objects the owner handles (the drop zone, imported-file cards) and for the single tinted verdict note; dashboard content is never wrapped in cards.

rules.name: The Only-Floating-Things-Cast Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is temporary and above the page". Anything that stays in the layout gets a hairline or a tone step instead.

dos: **Do** lead every analytical view with a sentence or a comparison (this period, last period, delta, same period last year) before any chart.
**Do** keep jade for the selected state, focus, and kept or saved money only (The One Jade Rule).
**Do** pair every up/down colour with a filled triangle and screen-reader "up"/"down" text (The Triangle-Plus-Tint Rule).
**Do** set tabular figures and en-IN grouping on every rupee value, with compact `k` / `L` / `Cr` on chart axes and labels.
**Do** separate sections and rows with 1px hairlines (`rule`, `rule-2`) on the paper ground.
**Do** give every chart a text equivalent (adjacent table or list plus tooltips) and make its marks keyboard reachable where they act as controls.
**Do** derive new category colours from the `oklch(0.68 0.1 <hue>)` formula and always print the category name beside its swatch.
**Do** label sample data as sample wherever it is shown.
donts: **Don't** wrap dashboard analysis in cards or tiles; boxed containers belong only to the drop zone, imported-file cards and the tinted verdict note.
**Don't** introduce four-up KPI tiles or donut charts; comparisons are tables with deltas, shares are horizontal bars.
**Don't** use persimmon for anything except overspend, errors or a negative balance effect.
**Don't** put shadows on resting surfaces; only the tooltip and toast float.
**Don't** use uppercase labels, letterspaced eyebrows or a second display face; hierarchy is size and weight in Anek Latin.
**Don't** saturate unselected chart series; resting data stays in its low-chroma tint.
**Don't** build metaphorical or retro-artifact visuals (ledger paper, terminals, timetables, signage); this is a modern finance dashboard.
**Don't** add a dark theme by inverting tokens; the system is defined light-only.
